newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 7.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--A show of strength from farmers last night as thousands of tractors broke through police lines to take over the national highway. The 2,500 tractors are ready at any moment to stop traffic on the national road in what will be a repeat of the 25-day December blockade. In response, the government issued a late night warning that any attempt to cut off traffic would be dealt with "decisively".
--The state will attempt a partial refinancing of old loans, exploiting more favourable lending coniditions in the international markets and the country's improved credit rating.

--The continuation of the three-week high school teachers' strike has made the extension of the school year more likely, with some proposing Saturday school and cancellation of traditional school trips. Everything however depends on how much longer teachers will stay out.

--Police arrested 28 people in an illegal betting racket late on Wednesday in raids in the greater Athens area. Illegal betting is estimated to have siphoned-off 16 billion drachmas from state-run games.
--Farmers in Thessaly are marching off to battle despite a dramatic announcement from the government last night that it would not allow them to block the roads.
--Conservative opposition leader Miltiades Evert has called for the resignation of bluntly-spoken Justice Minister Evangelos Yannopoulos and Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas.
--Police groups have condemned the "inhuman conditions" under which they are being forced to do duty in Thessaly, criticising the government for not paying them full overtime.

--Authorities examining the records of the illegal betting ring broken up on Wednesday night say they have found some famous names on the lists of those involved. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
